hook: A growing helical polymer picks the right mirror-image monomer far better than its catalyst alone does.
hook_turn: picks the right mirror-image monomer far better than its catalyst alone does.
summary: In a rhodium and chiral amine system, polymerizing racemic diazoacetates gets more selective as the chain grows and curls into a one-handed helix. The selectivity factor rises from 15 at 3% conversion to about 138 at 33%, then levels off. Computation on decamers supports helix-driven enantiomer recognition. The result is shown for one catalyst family and its monomers.
title: Dynamic Nonlinear Effects in the Asymmetric Kinetic Resolution Polymerization of Racemic Diazoacetates to One-Handed Helical Polycarbenes
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
